title: Rule record
description: A single proof obligation a delivery gate enforces against an AI coding agent's own claims about its work.

id.description: Stable identifier for the rule, written as a kebab-case slug. Used as the rule's file name and as a reference key from other tooling.

name.description: Human readable name for the rule. Exists because a bare identifier or number is not usable in a link or a conversation.

claim_class.description: The class of claim this rule governs, for example a robustness claim, a completeness claim, or a claim about review findings.

proof_obligation.description: What evidence a claim in this class must carry before it can be accepted as validated.

failure_mode.description: What goes wrong, concretely, when this rule is not followed.

origin_incident.description: The real event or documented failure pattern that motivates this rule. Where no single recorded event exists, this describes the recurring pattern instead of inventing one.

severity.description: How much damage this rule prevents when it fires, ranked from critical down to low. This ranks the rule itself and is a separate vocabulary from the severity a hook puts on an individual finding, which is why the two sets of values differ.

enforcement.description: The mechanism that enforces this rule: an automated hook, a prompt-level instruction, or a human review gate.

emits.description: Check ids the enforcing code emits for this rule. A record with an empty list is not checked mechanically. Every id a hook can emit belongs to exactly one record, so a finding can be traced back to the rule it came from.
